text:
In May of 2017 we said, over and over, "american health care act." One hundred and eighty-four of us reached the same five words on the same day, the fourth; one hundred and seventy-nine of us added the article and said "the american health care act." When we shortened it, sixty-three of us landed on "american health care act ahca," as if the parenthetical itself had been assigned.

Around the bill we arranged the familiar frame: sixty-five of us said "repeal and replace," and one hundred and eight of us spoke of those "with pre-existing conditions." Sixty-one of us named the "health care system" we meant to change.

We converged on the fourth, the day of the vote. What we were, that month, was one hundred and eighty-four voices holding one title. The record shows the title, and shows how many of us held it.
